narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the story of Joseph in Egypt; steady, warm storyteller.

joseph-the-patriarch.name: Joseph
joseph-the-patriarch.note: Jacob's son, about thirty to forty, governor of Egypt; wise and commanding, stern with his brothers while hiding deep emotion, tender when he reveals himself.

josephs-brothers.name: Joseph's brothers
josephs-brothers.note: The sons of Jacob speaking together; humble and frightened before the lord of Egypt, uneasy in conscience.

pharaoh.name: Pharao
pharaoh.note: King of Egypt; troubled by his dreams, then generous and regal toward Joseph.

jacob.name: Jacob
jacob.note: The aged patriarch, also called Israel; anxious, grieving for his lost sons, reluctant to let Benjamin go.

1.t: Joseph could no longer refrain himself before many that stood by: whereupon he commanded that all should go out, and no stranger be present at their knowing one another.

2.t: And he lifted up his voice with weeping, which the Egyptians, and all the house of Pharao heard.

3.t: And he said to his brethren:
I am Joseph: Is my father yet living?
His brethren could not answer him, being struck with exceeding great fear.

4.t: And he said mildly to them:
And when they were come near him, he said:
I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.

5.t: Be not afraid, and let it not seem to you a hard case that you sold me into these countries: for God sent me before you into Egypt for your preservation.

6.t: For it is two years since the famine began to be upon the land, and five years more remain, wherein there can be neither ploughing nor reaping.

7.t: And God sent me before, that you may be preserved upon the earth, and may have food to live.

8.t: Not by your counsel was I sent hither, but by the will of God: who hath made me as it were a father to Pharao, and lord of his whole house, and governor in all the land of Egypt.

9.t: Make haste, and go ye up to my father, and say to him: Thus saith thy son Joseph: God hath made me lord of the whole land of Egypt; come down to me, linger not.

10.t: And thou shalt dwell in the land of Gessen: and thou shalt be near me, thou and thy sons, and thy sons' sons, thy sheep, and thy herds, and all things that thou hast.

11.t: And there I will feed thee, (for there are yet five years of famine remaining) lest both thou perish, and thy house, and all things that thou hast.

12.t: Behold, your eyes, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, see that it is my mouth that speaketh to you.

13.t: You shall tell my father of all my glory, and all things that you have seen in Egypt: make haste and bring him to me.

14.t: And falling upon the neck of his brother Benjamin, he embraced him and wept: and Benjamin in like manner wept also on his neck.

15.t: And Joseph kissed all his brethren, and wept upon every one of them: after which they were emboldened to speak to him.

16.t: And it was heard, and the fame was spread abroad in the king's court: The brethren of Joseph are come; and Pharao with all his family was glad.
16.q: the rumour "The brethren of Joseph are come" is a report with no speaker; kept with the narrator

17.t: And he spoke to Joseph that he should give orders to his brethren, saying:
Load your beasts, and go into the land of Chanaan,

18.t: And bring away from thence your father and kindred, and come to me; and I will give you all the good things of Egypt, that you may eat the marrow of the land.

19.t: Give orders also that they take wagons out of the land of Egypt, for the carriage of their children and their wives; and say: Take up your father, and make haste to come with all speed:

20.t: And leave nothing of your household stuff; for all the riches of Egypt shall be yours.

21.t: And the sons of Israel did as they were bid. And Joseph gave them wagons according to Pharao's commandment: and provisions for the way.

22.t: He ordered also to be brought out for every one of them two robes: but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver, with five robes of the best:

23.t: Sending to his father as much money and raiment; adding besides, ten he-asses, to carry off all the riches of Egypt, and as many she-asses, carrying wheat and bread for the journey.

24.t: So he sent away his brethren, and at their departing said to them:
Be not angry in the way.

25.t: And they went up out of Egypt, and came into the land of Chanaan, to their father Jacob.

26.t: Joseph, thy son, is living; and he is ruler in all the land of Egypt.
Which when Jacob heard, he awaked as it were out of a deep sleep, yet did not believe them.

27.t: They, on the other side, told the whole order of the thing. And when he saw the wagons, and all that he had sent, his spirit revived,

28.t: It is enough for me if Joseph, my son, be yet living: I will go and see him before I die.
